correctness.rationale: Because a finite local nonfield has zero-divisor ideal \(\mathfrak m\), the classical total-graph structure theorem gives, after deleting zero, \(K_{s-1}\dot\cup(q-1)K_s\) if \(2\in\mathfrak m\), and \(K_{s-1}\dot\cup((q-1)/2)K_{s,s}\) otherwise. Zero forcing is additive over components, with \(Z(K_t)=t-1\) for \(t\ge2\), \(Z(K_{s,s})=2s-2\), and \(Z(K_1)=1\). Rank-one clique blocks and rank-two complete-bipartite blocks give a pattern matrix of rank \(q\) for \(s\ge3\); the boundary \(s=2\) has \(q=2\) and graph \(K_1\dot\cup K_2\), of real minimum rank one. Thus \(M\le Z\) closes the lower bound. Minimum sets omit exactly one allowed vertex per residue component, giving \((s-1)s^{q-1}\). Fresh direct residue-graph enumeration reproduced \((Z,\#\min)=(2,2),(5,12),(5,18)\) for \(\mathbb Z_4,\mathbb Z_8,\mathbb Z_9\).
correctness.risk: The theorem depends essentially on locality, since for nonlocal finite rings the zero divisors need not form an ideal.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete forcing and inverse-eigenvalue classification for an entire natural class, including a sharp small-ring boundary, every minimum forcing set, and recovery of the residue-field and maximal-ideal sizes from graph invariants. This goes beyond a single routine parameter substitution.

final_claim: For a finite commutative local nonfield \(R\), writing \(q=|R/\mathfrak m|\) and \(s=|\mathfrak m|\), the total graph with zero deleted satisfies \(Z=M=2\), \(\operatorname{mr}=1\) when \(s=2\), and \(Z=M=q(s-1)-1\), \(\operatorname{mr}=q\) when \(s\ge3\); moreover there are exactly \((s-1)s^{q-1}\) minimum zero forcing sets, characterized by residue-coset transversals.
